- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.30 over recent days), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast peak and introduce early downward slope.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.00–0.30), model frequently underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.0% buffer below forecast mean for next 5–7 days.
- Model overestimates short-term volatility when sentiment is volatile; smooth 30d forecast by averaging 7–14 day moving window.
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope slightly and delay peak by 1–3 days.
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, model tends to ignore it; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast mean for next 7 days.
- Forecast bias toward high values when sentiment is weakly positive; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment < 0.10.
